note.question: How do the economic impact of membership-based free shipping programs affect E-tailers?
note.overview: This research examines the economic impact of membership-based free-shipping (MFS) programs when introduced as an augmentation to widely accepted contingent free-shipping (CFS) policies. Under CFS, consumers waive the shipping surcharge if the order exceeds a certain threshold, whereas under MFS, consumers pay an upfront fee and enjoy the free-shipping perk throughout the membership period. The paper develops a stylized model that considers consumer heterogeneity in two dimensions: (1) disutility from acquiring an auxiliary product-a product that consumers would not otherwise purchase-to qualify for CFS; and (2) shopping frequency over a given period.

models.summary: This research examines the economic impact of membership-based free-shipping (MFS) programs when introduced as an augmentation to widely accepted contingent free-shipping (CFS) policies. Under CFS, consumers waive the shipping surcharge if the order exceeds a certain threshold, whereas under MFS, consumers pay an upfront fee and enjoy the free-shipping perk throughout the membership period. The paper's analysis suggests that the introduction of MFS allows the e-tailer to segment the market further, which could lead to a higher product price.
